fullPassage: The technical term often used to describe animals' judgement of numbers is the approximate number system. What it does not provide is precision. It shows — and this is the same in every species tested — a characteristic pattern of errors, with discrimination becoming less accurate as the quantities get bigger. Rhesus monkeys can tell one from two, two from three, three from four, four from five ... but start to fail from five upwards. Rats that learned to press a lever a given number of times, from four up to twenty-four, became markedly less and less precise in their responses as the number increased: by the top end of the range they would merely produce a spread of numbers around the target. It is a common observation that when testing the accuracy of animals' number sense, errors will increase with the size of the numbers.

It is a common __________ (observe) that when testing the accuracy of animals' number sense, errors will increase with the size of the numbers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: a common __________ that ~ : 관사 a와 형용사 common의 수식을 받는 명사 자리 → observe(동사)를 observation(명사)으로. It is a common observation that ~(~은 흔한 관찰 결과이다)

questions.passage: The technical term often used to describe animals' judgement of numbers is the approximate number system. What it does not provide is precision. It shows — and this is the same in every species tested — a characteristic pattern of errors, with discrimination becoming less accurate as the quantities get bigger. Rhesus monkeys can tell one from two, two from three, three from four, four from five ... but __________ from five upwards. Rats that learned to press a lever a given number of times, from four up to twenty-four, became markedly less and less precise in their responses as the number increased: by the top end of the range they would merely produce a spread of numbers around the target. It is a common observation that when testing the accuracy of animals' number sense, errors will increase with the size of the numbers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸 정답: start to fail(실패하기 시작하다) — 원숭이는 4까지는 구별하지만 5부터는 '실패하기 시작함'
det.analysis:
✅ ③ start to fail: 양이 커질수록 구별이 부정확해진다는 앞 내용과 일치 — but(그러나)으로 연결되어 능력의 한계를 보여줌
❌ ① begin to improve: 개선되기 시작하다 — 수가 커질수록 못하게 되므로 반대
❌ ② continue to succeed: 계속 성공하다 — but의 역접 흐름과 모순
❌ ④ refuse to count: 세기를 거부하다 — 능력의 한계이지 거부가 아님
det.tip: but start to fail from five upwards = 그러나 5부터는 실패하기 시작한다

questions.passage: The technical term often used to describe animals' judgement of numbers is the approximate number system. What it does not provide is precision. It shows — and this is the same in every species tested — a characteristic pattern of errors, with discrimination becoming less accurate as the quantities get bigger. Rhesus monkeys can tell one from two, two from three, three from four, four from five ... but start to fail from five upwards. Rats that learned to press a lever a given number of times, from four up to twenty-four, became markedly less and less precise in their responses as the number increased: by the top end of the range they would merely produce __________ around the target. It is a common observation that when testing the accuracy of animals' number sense, errors will increase with the size of the numbers.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸 정답: a spread of numbers(퍼져 있는 수들) — 범위 끝에서는 목표 주변에 '퍼진 수들'만 만들어 냄
det.analysis:
✅ ① a spread of numbers: 수가 커질수록 현저히 덜 정밀해졌으므로, 목표를 정확히 못 맞추고 그 주변에 퍼진 수들을 만들어 냄 — 원문 일치
❌ ② an exact count: 정확한 횟수 — 정밀함을 잃었다는 흐름과 반대
❌ ③ a single answer: 하나의 답 — 덜 정밀해졌다는 문맥과 모순
❌ ④ a fixed response: 고정된 반응 — 반응이 흔들린다는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: merely produce a spread of numbers around the target = 목표 주변에 퍼진 수들만 만들어 내다
